title: PySpark program stuck at adding broadcast piece
question:
I'm trying to write a PySpark program that filters for records in a very large dataframe (1-2B records) that matches some conditions on another smaller reference dataframe. This is done using a left join between the 2 dataframes, and then writing the results to a parquet file. When the reference dataframe is empty, the program runs successfully. But when the reference dataframe contains 414K records, the spark program hangs at the message storage.BlockManagerInfo: [dispatcher-BlockManagerMaster]: Added broadcast_4_piece0 in memory on xxx:12345 (size:4.0 MiB, free: 10 GiB).

My code is as follows.

def extract_to_df(spark, ref_db):
    columns_to_drop = ["ColA", "ColB", "ColC"]

    # Join conditions
    join_cond_1 = (col("Col1") >= col("Col3a")) & (col("Col1") >= col("Col3b"))
    join_cond_2 = (col("Col2") >= col("Col3a")) & (col("Col2") >= col("Col3b"))

    df = spark.read.parquet(folder)
    df_2 = df.filter(df["Col4"]=="abc").withColumn("Col1", udf_col(col("Col1a"))).withColumn("Col2", udf_col(col("Col2a")))

    df_tmp = df_2.join(ref_db, on=join_cond_1, how="left").drop(*columns_to_drop).withColumnRenamed("Col5", "Col5a")
    df_results = df_tmp.join(ref_db, on=join_cond_2, how="left").drop(*columns_to_drop).withColumnRenamed("Col6", "Col6a")
    df_final_results = df_results.dropna(subset=["Col5a", "Col6a"])

    df_final_results.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(output_folder)

def main():
    ref_db = spark.read.parquet("/ref_db.parquet")
    ref_db.persist()

    extract_to_df(spark, ref_db)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

What is wrong with the code?
answer:
The most effective solution is to disable the automatic broadcast join for your specific case. This forces Spark to use a more suitable join algorithm, like Sort-Merge Join, which is designed for joining large datasets and handles non-equi-joins more gracefully.

You can set the threshold to a very low value or to -1 to disable it completely.

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col

# Create a SparkSession
spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("DataFrameJoinIssue").getOrCreate()

# Disable automatic broadcast join
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "-1")

def extract_to_df(spark, ref_db):
    columns_to_drop = ["ColA", "ColB", "ColC"]

    join_cond_1 = (col("Col1") >= col("Col3a")) & (col("Col1") >= col("Col3b"))
    join_cond_2 = (col("Col2") >= col("Col3a")) & (col("Col2") >= col("Col3b"))

    df = spark.read.parquet("folder")
    df_2 = df.filter(df["Col4"]=="abc").withColumn("Col1", udf_col(col("Col1a"))).withColumn("Col2", udf_col(col("Col2a")))

    # Now Spark will use a Sort-Merge Join instead of a Broadcast Join
    df_tmp = df_2.join(ref_db, on=join_cond_1, how="left").drop(*columns_to_drop).withColumnRenamed("Col5", "Col5a")
    df_results = df_tmp.join(ref_db, on=join_cond_2, how="left").drop(*columns_to_drop).withColumnRenamed("Col6", "Col6a")
    df_final_results = df_results.dropna(subset=["Col5a", "Col6a"])

    df_final_results.write.mode("overwrite").parquet("output_folder")

def main():
    # Read and persist the reference data
    ref_db = spark.read.parquet("/ref_db.parquet")
    ref_db.persist()

    extract_to_df(spark, ref_db)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

By adding spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "-1") at the beginning of your code, you instruct Spark to use an alternative, more robust join strategy that can handle the volume of data without causing the program to hang.
